paper.title_en: Holevo-Bounded Total Information from Pair Distributions of Alternative Quantum Measurements
paper.abstract_en: The accessible information of a quantum ensemble can be strictly smaller than its Holevo information because a single-copy measurement may discard part of the label--system correlation. We ask whether information represented across two alternative measurement contexts can bridge this gap without assigning a joint distribution to their outcomes. Building on the relative-entropy-based projection method introduced by Harder et al., we define the directed posterior novelty of each record relative to the other, and an associated total-information quantity. For posterior-orthogonal records, this quantity equals the sum of the two record mutual informations. For finite-dimensional classical--quantum ensembles, we prove that optimizing this quantity over pairs of POVMs yields a value between the accessible and Holevo information. The upper bound follows by showing that the directed posterior novelty provides a lower bound on the infimum of the measured-relative-entropy recovery error. The uniform BB84 ensemble provides an example in which the quantity saturates the Holevo information while strictly exceeding the accessible information. Finally, we analytically establish the quantum validity of a redundancy-based information causality condition, resolving a question that has remained open since the condition was introduced.
